newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers Maxipime gets FDA clearance.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers Maxipime gets FDA clearance.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said Thursday its antibiotic Maxipime has received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the empiric treatment of febrile neutropenic patients.

Maxipime is an injectable, broad-spectrum antibiotic, the company said. It was cleared in January 1996 for the treatment of moderate-to-severe pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and uncomplicated skin and skin-structure infections.
Febrile neutropenia affects about 1.5 million U.S. patients, the company said. It is a condition in which fever occurs in patients with very low numbers of white blood cells, called neutrophils.

Persons suffering from the condition include patients who have received intensive chemotherapy or radiation, or those who suffer hematologic disorders that compromise their immune systems, the company said.
